statement: The function returns a result r (Ok r) and r is exactly the maximum, over all pairs of nodes u and v of root (including u = v), of the number of edges on the unique simple path from u to v, restricted to those paths on which every node has the same value as u; a single-node path has length 0. If root is Null (n = 0), the returned value is r = 0.
preconditions: root is a Tree with n nodes, where 0 <= n <= 10000; the depth of root is at most 1000; every node value is an integer in [-1000, 1000]. Here a node means an occurrence of the Node constructor.

statement: For every root satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result r and does not fail: there is no overflow, out-of-bounds access, or panic.
preconditions: root is a Tree with n nodes, where 0 <= n <= 10000; the depth of root is at most 1000; every node value is an integer in [-1000, 1000].

statement: Whenever the function returns r on root, 0 <= r <= max(0, n - 1), where n is the number of nodes of root.
preconditions: root is a Tree with n nodes, where 0 <= n <= 10000; the depth of root is at most 1000; every node value is an integer in [-1000, 1000].

statement: Whenever the function returns r on root, if root is nonempty then there exist nodes u and v of root (possibly u = v) such that the unique simple path from u to v has exactly r edges and every node on that path has the same value; if root is Null then r = 0.
preconditions: root is a Tree with n nodes, where 0 <= n <= 10000; the depth of root is at most 1000; every node value is an integer in [-1000, 1000].

statement: Whenever the function returns r on root, every simple path between two nodes of root whose nodes all have the same value has length at most r edges.
preconditions: root is a Tree with n nodes, where 0 <= n <= 10000; the depth of root is at most 1000; every node value is an integer in [-1000, 1000].

statement: Whenever the function returns r on root, r equals the maximum, over all pairs of nodes u and v of root, of the number of edges on the unique simple path from u to v; equivalently, r is the diameter of root measured in edges.
preconditions: root is nonempty and every node of root has the same value x, with -1000 <= x <= 1000 and 1 <= n <= 10000, where n is the number of nodes in root; the depth of root is at most 1000.

statement: Whenever the function returns r on root, r = 0 if and only if every parent-child edge of root joins two nodes with different values; equivalently, r > 0 if and only if there is at least one parent-child edge whose two endpoint values are equal.
preconditions: root is a Tree with n nodes, where 0 <= n <= 10000; the depth of root is at most 1000; every node value is an integer in [-1000, 1000].

statement: Whenever the function returns r on root, and rL is the result returned by the function on L when L is non-Null (with rL = 0 when L = Null), and rR is the result returned by the function on R when R is non-Null (with rR = 0 when R = Null), then r >= rL and r >= rR.
preconditions: root is a Tree of the form Node(x, L, R), with 0 <= n <= 10000 nodes, depth at most 1000, and every node value in [-1000, 1000]; L is the left subtree and R is the right subtree.

statement: Let mirror(root) be the tree obtained from root by recursively replacing every Node(x, L, R) with Node(x, mirror(R), mirror(L)) and leaving Null unchanged. Whenever the function returns r on root and r_m on mirror(root), r = r_m.
preconditions: root is a Tree with 0 <= n <= 10000 nodes, depth at most 1000, and every node value in [-1000, 1000].

statement: Whenever the function returns r on root and r_f on T_f(root), r = r_f.
preconditions: root is a Tree with 0 <= n <= 10000 nodes, depth at most 1000, and every node value in [-1000, 1000]. Let S be the set of values occurring in root. Let f be any function from S into [-1000, 1000] that is injective on S. Let T_f(root) be the tree obtained by replacing each node value v by f(v).

statement: Whenever the function returns r on root, and rL is the result returned by the function on L when L is non-Null (with rL = 0 when L = Null), and rR is the result returned by the function on R when R is non-Null (with rR = 0 when R = Null), then r = max(rL, rR).
preconditions: root is a Tree of the form Node(x, L, R), with 0 <= n <= 10000 nodes, depth at most 1000, and every node value in [-1000, 1000]; L is the left subtree and R is the right subtree; every non-null child of root has a root value different from x.

statement: If the function returns r on root, then r = max(rL, rR, armL + armR). Thus every longest univalue path is either wholly contained in one child subtree or is formed by joining through root the longest equal-valued downward arms in the left and right subtrees.
preconditions: root = Node(x, L, R) with 0 <= n <= 10000 nodes, depth at most 1000, and every node value in [-1000, 1000]; L and R are the left and right subtrees. For a nonempty tree w, define down(w) as the maximum number of edges on a downward path starting at w and following only child edges, all of whose nodes have the same value as the root of w; a single-node downward path has length 0. Let rL and rR be the function results on L and R when non-Null, and 0 when Null. Let armL = 0 if L = Null or root(L) has value different from x, otherwise armL = 1 + down(L); define armR similarly.
